title: Directions and transportation
goal: Asking for directions and understanding the answer, riding the MTR, buses, minibuses, and taxis, and building “take X to Y” sentences in the right Cantonese order.
bekal: ask the way: 點去 and 喺邊度
give directions: 直行, 轉左, 轉右, 對面
build sentences with 搭 + vehicle + 去 + place
the must-know phrases for Hong Kong taxis and minibuses

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — Lost in Central
dialogs.intro: Andi loses his way in Central and asks a passerby. Notice that Hongkongers' answers are usually short and full of motion verbs — not long explanations.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唔該|M4 goi1]，[請問|cing2 man6][中環站|Zung1 waan4 zaam6][喺邊度呀|hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
lines.id: Excuse me, where's Central station?
lines.literal: excuse-me, please — ask — Central — station — at — which — place — huh.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [你直行|Nei5 zik6 haang4]，[過咗個街口|gwo3 zo2 go3 gaai1 hau2][轉左|zyun3 zo2]。
lines.id: Go straight, and turn left after the intersection.
lines.literal: you — straight — walk, pass — already — classifier — street — mouth — turn — left.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [轉左之後呢|Zyun3 zo2 zi1 hau6 ne1]？
lines.id: And after I turn left?
lines.literal: turn — left — after — how-about.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [行多兩分鐘|Haang4 do1 loeng5 fan1 zung1]，[喺銀行對面|hai2 ngan4 hong4 deoi3 min6]。
lines.id: Walk two more minutes; it's across from the bank.
lines.literal: walk — more — two — minute, at — bank — facing — side.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [遠唔遠呀|Jyun5 m4 jyun5 aa3]？[使唔使搭車|Sai2 m4 sai2 daap3 ce1]？
lines.id: Is it far? Do I need to take something?
lines.literal: far — not — far — huh. need — not — need — ride — vehicle.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [唔使|M4 sai2]，[好近|hou2 kan5]，[行五分鐘就到|haang4 ng5 fan1 zung1 zau6 dou3]。
lines.id: No need, it's close — five minutes on foot.
lines.literal: not — need, filler — close, walk — five — minute — then — arrive.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [多謝晒|Do1 ze6 saai3]！[哦|O4]，[仲有|zung6 jau5] — [我想去尖沙咀|ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 Zim1 saa1 zeoi2]，[點去呀|dim2 heoi3 aa3]？
lines.id: Thanks so much! Oh, one more thing — I want to go to Tsim Sha Tsui. How do I get there?
lines.literal: thanks — completely. oh, still — have — I — would-like — go — Tsim-Sha-Tsui, how — go — huh.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [搭地鐵啦|Daap3 dei6 tit3 laa1]。[中環轉車|Zung1 waan4 zyun3 ce1]，[坐兩個站就到|co5 loeng5 go3 zaam6 zau6 dou3]。
lines.id: Just take the MTR. Change trains at Central; it's two stops.
lines.literal: ride — under-ground — iron — go-on. Central — turn — vehicle, sit — two — classifier — station — then — arrive.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [要幾耐呀|Jiu3 gei2 noi6 aa3]？
lines.id: How long does it take?
lines.literal: need — how — long — huh.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [大概|Daai6 koi3][十分鐘啦|sap6 fan1 zung1 laa1]。[搭船都得|Daap3 syun4 dou1 dak1]，[但係慢啲|daan6 hai6 maan6 di1]。
lines.id: About ten minutes. You can take the ferry too, but it's slower.
lines.literal: roughly — roughly — ten — minute — go-on. ride — boat — also — OK, but — slow — a-bit.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [咁我搭船|Gam2 ngo5 daap3 syun4]！[我想睇下個海|Ngo5 soeng2 tai2 haa5 go3 hoi2]。
lines.id: Then I'll take the ferry! I want to see the sea.
lines.literal: so — I — ride — boat. I — would-like — see — a-bit — classifier — sea.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [好主意|Hou2 zyu2 ji3]！[碼頭喺嗰邊|Maa5 tau4 hai2 go2 bin1]。
lines.id: Good idea! The pier is over there.
lines.literal: good — main — idea. pier — at — that — side.

notes: **[喺|hai2] = at, in.** This is the native Cantonese word for location (Mandarin uses 在), and from now on it will appear in almost every sentence. ⚠️ Don't confuse it with [係|hai6] “to be” from Unit 1 — different character (喺 has 口 on the left), different tone (2 vs 6), different meaning.

**[直行|zik6 haang4] = go straight, [轉左|zyun3 zo2] = turn left, [轉右|zyun3 jau6] = turn right.** [行|haang4] is the Cantonese word for walking; Mandarin uses 走. ⚠️ In Cantonese, [走|zau2] actually means “leave, run off”, not walk.
**[街口|gaai1 hau2] = “street mouth”, i.e. an intersection.** The character [口|hau2] (mouth) is used for any opening: [出口|ceot1 hau2] (exit), [入口|jap6 hau2] (entrance), [門口|mun4 hau2] (doorway).
**[使唔使|sai2 m4 sai2]？ = “do I need to?”** The A-唔-A form of [使|sai2] (need). The answer is [使|Sai2] or [唔使|M4 sai2]. 🇭🇰 You'll hear this far more often than 需唔需要.
**[就|zau6] marks “then, right away, just”.** [行五分鐘就到|Haang4 ng5 fan1 zung1 zau6 dou3] = walk five minutes and you're there. It links a condition to its result and stands before the second verb.

**[坐|co5] is used to “ride” a vehicle you sit in, [搭|daap3] for any public transportation.** They're often interchangeable: [搭地鐵|daap3 dei6 tit3] and [坐地鐵|co5 dei6 tit3] are both correct. 🇭🇰 搭 is more common in Hong Kong.

**[幾耐|gei2 noi6] = how long.** Compare [幾時|gei2 si4] (when) from Unit 1 — one asks about duration, the other about a point in time. [好耐|hou2 noi6] = a long time; [好耐冇見|hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3] = long time no see.

grammars.title: 搭 + vehicle + 去 + place
body: To say “go somewhere by something”, Cantonese builds it in exactly that order: **the means first, the destination after**. English puts the destination first (“go to Mongkok by MTR”), and this is where learners trip up most in this unit.

head: Cantonese
Meaning
rows: [我搭地鐵去旺角|Ngo5 daap3 dei6 tit3 heoi3 Wong6 gok3]。
I go to Mongkok by MTR.
[佢搭巴士返工|Keoi5 daap3 baa1 si2 faan1 gung1]。
He goes to work by bus.
[我哋搭的士去機場|Ngo5 dei6 daap3 dik1 si2 heoi3 gei1 coeng4]。
We go to the airport by taxi.
[我行路返屋企|Ngo5 haang4 lou6 faan1 uk1 kei2]。
[搭咩車去呀|Daap3 me1 ce1 heoi3 aa3]？
What do you take to get there?

head: Wrong
Right
rows: [我搭地鐵去旺角|Ngo5 daap3 dei6 tit3 heoi3 Wong6 gok3]。
[我搭巴士返工|Ngo5 daap3 baa1 si2 faan1 gung1]。

after: **If a time is mentioned too, it still goes first**: [我聽日搭地鐵去旺角|Ngo5 ting1 jat6 daap3 dei6 tit3 heoi3 Wong6 gok3]。 The full order: time → means → verb → destination.

**[去|heoi3] moves away from the speaker, [嚟|lei4] moves toward, [返|faan1] goes back to a regular place.** [你去唔去呀|Nei5 heoi3 m4 heoi3 aa3]？ (are you going) · [佢嚟緊|Keoi5 lei4 gan2] (he's on his way here) · [我返屋企|Ngo5 faan1 uk1 kei2] (I'm going home).
⚠️ **Walking is [行路|haang4 lou6], not 走路.** If you say 我走路去, Hongkongers will understand you but hear Mandarin.

grammars.title: Direction and position words
body: Nearly all Cantonese position words end in [邊|bin1] (side) or [面|min6] (face). They come **after** the reference object — the reverse of English.

head: Cantonese
Meaning
Structure
rows: [喺銀行對面|hai2 ngan4 hong4 deoi3 min6]

after: ⚠️ **The order is the reverse of English.** We say “across from the bank”; Cantonese says “bank across”. Read it back to front until it feels natural.
**[隔籬|gaak3 lei4] is the native Cantonese word for “next to”** and doesn't exist in Mandarin. [隔籬屋|gaak3 lei4 uk1] = the house next door; [坐我隔籬|co5 ngo5 gaak3 lei4] = sit next to me.

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Taking a taxi
dialogs.intro: Andi takes a taxi to Tsim Sha Tsui. Hong Kong taxi talk is short and full of set phrases — learn these four or five and you'll be fine anywhere.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [師傅|Si1 fu2]，[去尖沙咀|heoi3 Zim1 saa1 zeoi2][唔該|m4 goi1]。
lines.id: Tsim Sha Tsui, please.
lines.literal: master — sir, go — Tsim-Sha-Tsui — please.

lines.speaker: 司機:
lines.text: [尖沙咀邊度呀|Zim1 saa1 zeoi2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？
lines.id: Which part of Tsim Sha Tsui?
lines.literal: Tsim-Sha-Tsui — which — place — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [彌敦道|Nei4 deon1 dou6]，[近地鐵站嗰度|kan5 dei6 tit3 zaam6 go2 dou6]。
lines.id: Nathan Road, near the MTR station.
lines.literal: Nathan — road, near — MTR — station — that — place.

lines.speaker: 司機:
lines.text: [好|Hou2]。[而家|Ji4 gaa1][有啲塞車|jau5 di1 sak1 ce1][喎|wo3]。
lines.id: OK. The traffic's a bit heavy right now.
lines.literal: OK. now — have — a-bit — jammed — vehicle — you-know.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唔緊要|M4 gan2 jiu3]。[大概要幾耐呀|Daai6 koi3 jiu3 gei2 noi6 aa3]？
lines.id: No problem. About how long will it take?
lines.literal: not — important. roughly — roughly — need — how — long — huh.

lines.speaker: 司機:
lines.text: [二十分鐘啦|Ji6 sap6 fan1 zung1 laa1]。[你係邊度嚟㗎|Nei5 hai6 bin1 dou6 lei4 gaa3]？
lines.id: About twenty minutes. Where are you from?
lines.literal: two — ten — minute — go-on. you — are — which — place — come — emphasis.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [印尼|Jan3 nei4]。[我嚟咗兩個月|Ngo5 lei4 zo2 loeng5 go3 jyut6]。
lines.id: Indonesia. I've been here two months.
lines.literal: Indonesia. I — come — already — two — classifier — month.

lines.speaker: 司機:
lines.text: [你廣東話唔錯喎|Nei5 Gwong2 dung1 waa2 m4 co3 wo3]！
lines.id: Your Cantonese isn't bad!
lines.literal: you — Cantonese — language — not — wrong — you-know.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [多謝|Do1 ze6]！[我學緊|Ngo5 hok6 gan2]。[前面|Cin4 min6][有落|jau5 lok6][唔該|m4 goi1]！
lines.id: Thanks! I'm learning. I'll get off up ahead!
lines.literal: thanks. I — learn — -ing. front — side — have — get-off — please.

lines.speaker: 司機:
lines.text: [好|Hou2]。[一共|Jat1 gung6][八十五蚊|baat3 sap6 ng5 man1]。
lines.id: OK. That's eighty-five dollars.
lines.literal: OK. one — together — eight — ten — five — dollar.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [呢度一百|Ni1 dou6 jat1 baak3]，[唔使找喇|m4 sai2 zaau2 laa3]。[多謝師傅|Do1 ze6 si1 fu2]！
lines.id: Here's a hundred — keep the change. Thank you!
lines.literal: this — place — one — hundred, not — need — change — already. thanks — master — sir.

notes: **[師傅|si1 fu2] is how you address taxi drivers, tradespeople, and any skilled worker.** Literally “master, expert”. 🇭🇰 Calling a taxi driver 師傅 instantly makes you sound local; calling him 先生 sounds odd.

**[有落|jau5 lok6]！ = “getting off!”** A must on minibuses, and also used in taxis. Say it fairly loudly, about ten seconds before your stop. 🇭🇰 On a green minibus, if you don't shout 有落, the driver won't stop — there's no button.
**[有啲|jau5 di1] = “a bit, somewhat”.** [有啲塞車|jau5 di1 sak1 ce1] = traffic's a bit heavy; [有啲攰|jau5 di1 gui6] = a bit tired. A very common softener.
**[唔錯|m4 co3] = “not bad”, and it's a real compliment.** Hongkongers rarely gush; 唔錯 already means good. Reply with just [多謝|Do1 ze6] or [邊有呀|Bin1 jau5 aa3] (“oh, not really”, modestly).

**[嚟咗兩個月|lei4 zo2 loeng5 go3 jyut6] = have been here two months.** Duration comes **after** the verb, unlike time words, which come before. Compare: [我琴日嚟|Ngo5 kam4 jat6 lei4] (I came yesterday) vs [我嚟咗兩日|Ngo5 lei4 zo2 loeng5 jat6] (I've been here two days).
**[學緊|hok6 gan2] = am learning.** [緊|gan2] attaches after a verb to mark an action in progress. 🔁 This is a preview of Unit 9; for now, just recognize the form.
🇭🇰 **Tipping in Hong Kong taxis: just round up.** [唔使找喇|M4 sai2 zaau2 laa3] = keep the change. There's no fixed percentage; rounding up a few dollars is already polite.

grammars.title: Motion verbs: 上, 落, 入, 出, 過
body: These five short verbs cover nearly every movement you need to talk about day to day, and all of them can stand alone or attach to another verb.

head: Word
Meaning
Example
rows: [上車|soeng5 ce1] get on a vehicle · [上樓|soeng5 lau2] go upstairs
[落車|lok6 ce1] get off · [落雨|lok6 jyu5] it's raining
[入去|jap6 heoi3] go in · [入閘|jap6 zaap6] go through the MTR gate
[出街|ceot1 gaai1] go out · [出閘|ceot1 zaap6] exit through the gate
[過馬路|gwo3 maa5 lou6] cross the road · [過海|gwo3 hoi2] cross the harbor

after: 🇭🇰 **[過海|gwo3 hoi2] is an everyday word in Hong Kong** — crossing between Hong Kong Island and Kowloon. Taxis charge extra for it, and some drivers refuse passengers who want to 過海 at the end of their shift.
**The order of combinations: main verb + direction + 去/嚟.** [行入去|haang4 jap6 heoi3] = walk + in + there. The three parts always come in this order.

sections.title: The MTR and Hong Kong transportation

blocks.text: Hong Kong has a dense public transportation network, and nearly all of it is paid for with one card: 八達通 (Octopus). You'll use the words below every day.

head: Vehicle
Cantonese
Note
rows: Its official name is 港鐵, but people still say 地鐵
Sit up front on the top deck — the best view
Fixed route, pay when you get on
Flexible route, pay when you get off, you must shout [有落|jau5 lok6]
Red = urban · green = New Territories · blue = Lantau
Only on Hong Kong Island, cheap and slow
The Star Ferry crosses the harbor
To the airport, 24 minutes from Central

head: On the MTR
Meaning
rows: [邊個站落呀|Bin1 go3 zaam6 lok6 aa3]？
Which station do I get off at?
[要唔要轉車呀|Jiu3 m4 jiu3 zyun3 ce1 aa3]？
Do I need to change trains?
[喺金鐘轉車|Hai2 Gam1 zung1 zyun3 ce1]。
[坐幾多個站呀|Co5 gei2 do1 go3 zaam6 aa3]？
[行邊個出口呀|Haang4 bin1 go3 ceot1 hau2 aa3]？
[八達通冇錢喇|Baat3 daat6 tung1 mou5 cin2 laa3]。
My Octopus card is out of credit.

blocks.title: The Hong Kong place names you'll hear most
items: [中環|Zung1 waan4] Central · [金鐘|Gam1 zung1] Admiralty · [銅鑼灣|Tung4 lo4 waan1] Causeway Bay · [灣仔|Waan1 zai2] Wan Chai
[尖沙咀|Zim1 saa1 zeoi2] Tsim Sha Tsui · [旺角|Wong6 gok3] Mongkok · [油麻地|Jau4 maa4 dei2] Yau Ma Tei · [深水埗|Sam1 seoi2 bou2] Sham Shui Po
[九龍|Gau2 lung4] Kowloon · [新界|San1 gaai3] New Territories · [大嶼山|Daai6 jyu4 saan1] Lantau
⚠️ The English spellings of Hong Kong place names were made over a century ago and are often far from their Jyutping sound. Rely on the characters and Jyutping, not the English spelling.

wave: Five minutes before Unit 7: open a map on your phone, pick two places you know in your own city, and explain the way in Cantonese — 直行, 轉左, 過馬路, 喺…對面. Then say how you get to work or school with the pattern 搭 + vehicle + 去 + place, and make sure the time word from Unit 5 goes first.
